'''Racuszki''' are [[Cookbook:Pancake|pancakes]] made from [[Cookbook:Batter|batter]] fried on a hot griddle or a pan. They are a traditional Polish dish, but they exist in several variations in many different local [[Cookbook:Cuisine|cuisine]]s, such as Danish [http://xphiles.typepad.com/table/2006/04/easter_ebleskiv.html|Ebleskivers]. Usually the form varies from small pancakes or something akin to donuts, and the filling can change as well (e.g. apple and cinnamon, raisins, etc.).

==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Liter|L]] sour milk or cultured [[Cookbook:Buttermilk|buttermilk]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] white [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
*1½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|baking soda]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Eggs|eggs]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Kg|kg]] [[Cookbook:Apple|apples]] (optional), [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] ground [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] (optional)
*½ cup [[Cookbook:Raisin|raisins]] (optional)

==Procedure==
#In large bowl, [[Cookbook:Mix|mix]] the baking soda, salt, and flour together well.
#Add sour milk and eggs, and [[Cookbook:Mix|mix]] until smooth.
#Pour small ladlefuls of the mixture into a [[Cookbook:Non-stick|non-stick]] pan, one at a time OR dip slices of peeled apples in batter and put them in the pan.
#Cook until the edges are dry. Turn; cook until golden.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* Serve with sugar, butter, maple syrup, melted chocolate, or jam. Sugar is traditional, and some people eat them without toppings.
* Racuszki do not store well.
* Use [[Cookbook:Yogurt|yogurt]] or cultured [[Cookbook:Buttermilk|buttermilk]] if you do not have sour milk, but do not replace it with normal milk.
* Cooking apples are preferred, if using.
